title: Denormalized State Updates in Separate Transactions
pattern: Writing primary records to a database table and updating a corresponding denormalized field or aggregate counter in a separate database connection transaction.
why_bad: Without atomic enforcement spanning both updates, any crash, timeout, or query failure that occurs between the two transactions leaves the database in a permanently inconsistent state (e.g., an email exists but the unread counter is 0) [134, 135]. This compromises database integrity and forces developers to write complex, slow reconciliation scripts to clean up mismatched states [134, 135].
detection: Identify consecutive database transaction blocks inside a single function where the first writes or deletes a record and the second updates a denormalized counter or balance related to that exact record.
fix: Combine both writes into a single, atomic database transaction so they either both succeed or both fail together, maintaining strict internal consistency [134, 135].
source: Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 7 (Acid - Atomicity) / passages [134, 135].
